answer: Each voyage epoch every agent publishes a signed lantern beacon bound to a burned bond; the inlet gateway checks the signature, verifies the bond is unspent, and admits the identity only if its beacon hash meets that epoch's proof-of-work target. An attacker forging N sybils must burn N separate bonds and recompute N PoW hashes per epoch, so every fake identity costs irrecoverable capital plus compute that grows linearly with the attack.
